newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan denies ships collided near disputed island.
newsitem.headline: Japan denies ships collided near disputed island.

text.p: Japan's Maritime Safety Agency on Monday denied Taiwanese media reports that said a ship carrying protesters from Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau who landed on disputed East China Sea islands had collided with a Japanese patrol boat.
The agency said it had been unable to confirm Taiwanese media reports that a Hong Kong citizen was missing.

"There have been reports that a Hong Kong citizen is missing and that a fishing boat had collided with a patrol boat and sunk, but officials have not confirmed this. There has been no collision between a fishing boat and patrol boat," it said in a statement.

Earlier, Taiwan's state radio quoted the captain of a Taiwanese protest boat as saying that a Japanese patrol boat butted the stern of his vessel early on Monday near the disputed islands, causing slight damage.

Japan's maritime agency confirmed that four protesters from Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau landed on the Senkaku Islands, known as the Diaoyu islands in Chinese, and had placed Chinese flags on the islands. It said the flags had fallen down or were washed away.
